Dream Labs opens Dream-1 robot API alongside $90 million seed funding

The model targets transfer to unfamiliar two-arm robots, but remains a research beta with embodiment-dependent limitations.

AI Brief ↗19 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Model access through an API

Dream Labs emerged with $90 million in seed funding led by B Capital and Kindred Ventures and opened Dream API to connect observations and language instructions to robot actions. Its technical documentation prices Dream-1 inference at $3 per hour and the flash version at $2. Those figures are not the purchase or total operating cost of a robot.

A shared gripper-level interface

The technical explanation describes predicting end-effector poses and gripper opening, then using each robot’s inverse-kinematics solver to produce joint commands. This supports transfer among bimanual parallel-gripper robots, using a head camera and two wrist cameras. It should not be interpreted as immediate support for every robot architecture.

Demonstrations have boundaries

Examples include manipulation and laundry folding, but the company acknowledges dependence on IK quality, workspace and mechanical differences. A fine-tuning service uses robot-specific data when zero-shot performance is insufficient. Dream-1 remains a research beta that can make mistakes and has not been validated for safety-critical use.
